source: fccb30810 (2026-11-05) transfer of the P/08 N4 refusal tables into forms/refusals.tsv; judge P08.25 M1 (sentence rewritten: the cells are normative text, a repeated row number selects one condition)
removed: Original normative cells are preserved; repeated row numbers select the original condition and its operation-specific projection.
In output, an array of objects is in the order of the key named in the form.
An order of selection (for example, the keepers of [P/08.8](08.8-domain.norms.md) N1.5) is not an order of\noutput.
Output, for the order of output arrays, is a view, door answers, functions of N5, written rows and objects.

The other rows of the holder are written only by the `domain` process (N1.8 `writer`): each one\nby the owner chapter of the lesson per the catalogue, with the turn guard ([chapter 8.10](08.10-domain.norms.md) N1.7 `guard`).
The doors of class `signed` the process serves over TLS with the server certificate of the role `domain` (N1.6).
The role set of the process is `domain` ([P/02.4 N1.6](../../02-installer/spec/02.4-installer.norms.md); the roles\nof processes — P/10 N1.4 `roles`).
On the listener of the `domain` process, identity is by the norm of the route (signature, token, password).

Under TLS the listener checks a presented client certificate in the handshake: the leaf chains to its own ca.pem or\nca.next.pem, the validity period holds, there is no extendedKeyUsage without `clientAuth`; otherwise — an alert, no HTTP.
`pass`: the method, the path\nwith query, the body, `Authorization`, `Idempotency-Key`, `If-Match` come to the process as they came.
The form of the values and the words of the versions and the repeat memory are [P/06.1](../../06-console/spec/06.1-console.norms.md) N2 «Versions», N3 «repeat memory».

The only difference of the doors of the process from the cluster console: the rows of the holder have\none writer ([chapter 8.10](08.10-domain.norms.md) N1.7), so a claim needs neither `pending` nor a takeover.
- An existing row without the field `revision` or with an unreadable field is unreadable by its current family; it is not revision 0 and a write does not normalize it to 1.
- For the field `revision`, confirmed absence and creation at revision 1, explicit corruption deletion and restoration from a current readable copy keep their existing rules.

- `ETag` is carried by the answers of success per the table [forms/versioned-doors.tsv](../forms/versioned-doors.tsv) and by the read doors of the domain console ([P/10](../../10-domain-console/spec/10-domain-console.norms.md) N1.2).

- The listings `GET /domain/users`, `GET /domain/groups`, `GET /domain/roles`, `GET /domain/break-glass`, `GET /domain/placement`, `GET /domain/grants` do not carry the header `ETag`: they have many rows, the index and `revision` stand at each row.
- Apart from the explicit folder and membership success bodies of P/08.5 N1.8, write success bodies do not carry the index: it becomes known only after the batch (below).
- Another value of `If-Match` — 400 `If-Match is a unit revision` before the row is read.
- After a `cas` conflict the condition is judged again, by the re-read row.
- Neither a numeric condition nor a matching store index turns a row whose `revision` does not read into a readable row.
- An explicit corruption-deletion path still follows its own stated procedure.
- The doors of the table [forms/versioned-doors.tsv](../forms/versioned-doors.tsv) require a right above `view`, so in `412 revision moved` `row` is present if there is a row and it reads.
The `optional-index` condition of membership accepts an absent If-Match or a double-quoted store index, including `""` for confirmed absence.
For membership, a bare number or another spelling of If-Match is 400 `If-Match is a store index`, before reading the row.
For membership, unknown reading is 503 unavailable, never index `""`.
For membership, the ordinary right check and response ceiling still apply.
An empty membership PUT deletes the row and returns `{folders: [], index: ""}`.
The doors `PUT /domain/topology` and `PUT /domain/shared` read `base_rev` only if there is no header `If-Match`, and then the refusal is the former one: 409 of the revision.

At `PUT /domain/topology` and `PUT /domain/shared`, both `If-Match` and `base_rev` are present: `<revision>` equals `base_rev` — the door judges `If-Match`; not equal, or an index stands next to `base_rev` — 400 `refused`, `field: /base_rev`: a counter and an index cannot be compared without the row, and the door does not guess an edit with two different conditions.

Neither `If-Match` nor `base_rev` is present — the former 400: at the doors `PUT /domain/topology` and `PUT /domain/shared` an omitted field stays as it was, so an edit without a condition is not written.
`key`: user — the name proven by the token (chapter 8.4 N1.5); path — the whole path of the door, `/domain/…`, the segments percent-decoded.
`print`: the print — who, method, path, body as a JSON value; no body — as `{}`.
`print`: the value — the HMAC print of chapter P/06.2 N1 under the holder's ring: the bodies of the people doors carry a password,\na bare hash would open a brute force past PBKDF2.
`print`: the ring does not read — 503 `unavailable`.
`memory`: the row does not read or the read\nis not confirmed — 503 `unavailable`, the row is not touched.
`in_flight`: a change of process leaves no work: the target and the answer land in one batch.
`write`: guards — `domain/signer-turn`\nof my version and the guards of the door (of references, of the administrator's proof, of the target status; chapter 8.4 N1.3, N1.3c, N3) in the same batch.
`refusal`: 5xx is not remembered.

`replay`: `ETag` — by the table [forms/versioned-doors.tsv](../forms/versioned-doors.tsv): the field `index`, otherwise the index of the claim row itself: all rows of a batch get one version (P/01.1 N1).
`replay`: a repeat writes nothing, there is no log.
`weight`: a 412 with `row` — first without `row` (P/06.1 N2 «Versions»).

A repeat goes through the pass anew and judges by the state: `DELETE /domain/users/<name>`, whose former pass removed the person's row, answers 404, and the grant rows are finished by the reconciliation (chapter 8.4 N3).
The chapter has no procedure of its own. The order at each door is N3 of the door in its chapter.
The client chooses the action by the word and puts the error at a field\nby `field`, without parsing the text for people.
- A door speaks only the words of its own rows of the closed list and of the rows `*` with the same code.
- The words of the present N4 stay, there is no renaming.
- The phrases in quotes of the N4 tables are the `detail` of the word `refused`, unless the row names them as the `error` word.
- `field` is present only at 400, 409 and 412 and\n  only at rows of the list where the column `field` is not `-`; a refusal not about a field is without it.
- The outcome\n  `conflict` (412) of applying a stored edit is seen in `outcomes` (chapter 8.6 N4).
